value.behaviour: getLassoSelectedElementIds takes an optional boxSelectionMode (default "overlap"); "overlap" runs today's enclosure-or-crossing algorithm unchanged, "contain" selects only elements whose whole outline (and whole positioned label) is inside the lasso polygon and not crossed by the lasso path.
rules: 1. Imports: add getElementLineSegments and isBoundToContainer to the existing `@excalidraw/element` import (names kept alphabetical); add LineSegment and Polygon to the existing `@excalidraw/math/types` type import; add a new last import `import type { AppState } from "../types";` separated by a blank line from the package type imports. No other import changes.

2. Input type gains `boxSelectionMode?: AppState["boxSelectionMode"];` after simplifyDistance; the destructuring gains `boxSelectionMode = "overlap",` after simplifyDistance. The return type and value stay `{ selectedElementIds: string[] }` built as `[...intersectedElements, ...enclosedElements]`.
3. Simplification, the unlockedElements filter, the two clear() calls and the lassoBounds reduce stay exactly as they are and in the same order.

4. After lassoBounds and before the element loop, build the Wrap inputs once: `const wrapLasso = boxSelectionMode === "contain" && path.length > 0 ? { polygon: polygonFromPoints(path), segments: getLassoSegments(path) } : null;` (from the simplified `path`).

5. The element loop keeps the same AABB pre-filter condition (doBoundsIntersect(lassoBounds, elementBounds) and not already in either set). Inside it: when boxSelectionMode === "contain", add element.id to enclosedElements only if `!isBoundToContainer(element) && wrapLasso && wrapTest(wrapLasso.polygon, wrapLasso.segments, element, elementsMap, elementsSegments)`; never add to intersectedElements in this branch. Otherwise (overlap) run today's code verbatim: enclosureTest, then intersectionTest only when not enclosed.

6. New module-private `const getLassoSegments = (lassoPath: GlobalPoint[]): LineSegment<GlobalPoint>[]` returns the consecutive segments `lineSegment(lassoPath[index], point)` over `lassoPath.slice(1)` followed by the closing segment `lineSegment(lassoPath[lassoPath.length - 1], lassoPath[0])`, exactly the expression intersectionTest uses today.
7. intersectionTest's `const lassoSegments = ...` expression becomes `const lassoSegments = getLassoSegments(lassoPath);`; the rest of intersectionTest and all of enclosureTest are unchanged.

8. New module-private `const isOutlineInside = (segments: LineSegment<GlobalPoint>[], lassoPolygon: Polygon<GlobalPoint>): boolean` returns false for an empty array, else true only when every point of every segment satisfies polygonIncludesPointNonZero(point, lassoPolygon).

9. New module-private `const isCrossedByLasso = (element: ExcalidrawElement, elementsMap: ElementsMap, lassoSegments: LineSegment<GlobalPoint>[]): boolean` returns true when some lasso segment gives `intersectElementWithLineSegment(element, elementsMap, lassoSegment, 0, true).length > 0`.

10. New module-private `const wrapTest = (lassoPolygon: Polygon<GlobalPoint>, lassoSegments: LineSegment<GlobalPoint>[], element: ExcalidrawElement, elementsMap: ElementsMap, elementsSegments: ElementsSegmentsMap): boolean`, evaluated in this order: (a) segments = elementsSegments.get(element.id); return false when undefined; (b) return false unless isOutlineInside(segments, lassoPolygon); (c) return false when isCrossedByLasso(element, elementsMap, lassoSegments); (d) boundTextElement = getBoundTextElement(element, elementsMap); when it is null return true; (e) positionedLabel = `{ ...boundTextElement, ...computeBoundTextPosition(element, boundTextElement, elementsMap) }`; return false unless isOutlineInside(getElementLineSegments(positionedLabel, elementsMap), lassoPolygon); (f) return !isCrossedByLasso(positionedLabel, elementsMap, lassoSegments).

11. The new helpers are appended after intersectionTest as `const` arrow functions; none is exported. Add no comments beyond one short line above wrapTest stating it implements the Wrap (contain) rule.
